title: Digit reversal — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 29 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 8. Most binding: reverseNum (8), isPrime (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: z9plus.lean. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/reversal.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to 3b083fac-92a3-8d45-a737-199fd51e8f0e. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 3, 1, 7, 7, 7, 5). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: address.lean (3 observed, 1.51 expected, lift 1.99), families.lean (7 observed, 3.73 expected, lift 1.88), energy.lean (3 observed, 1.86 expected, lift 1.61). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.57; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.49. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 91.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. digit reversal and digit sums; casting out nines, in use by the 12th century Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. reversal_preserves_digit_sum — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => digitSum (reverseNum n) == digitSum n) record
  2. digital_root_is_invariant_under_reversal — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => (reverseNum n) % 9 == n % 9) record
  3. the_ledger_reversal_cases — (reverseNum 12) % 9 == 12 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 45) % 9 == 45 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 123) % 9 == 123 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 1234) % 9 == 1234 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 4321) % 9 == 4321 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 9080) % 9 == 9080 % 9 record
  4. reversal_is_not_the_identity — ¬ ((List.range' 10 90).all (fun n => reverseNum n == n)) record
  5. palindromes_are_the_fixed_points — ((List.range' 10 90).filter (fun n => reverseNum n == n)).length = 9 record
  6. emirps_exist_below_one_hundred — ((List.range' 10 90).filter (fun n => isPrime n && isPrime (reverseNum n) && reverseNum n != n)).length > 0 record
  7. reversal_does_not_preserve_primality — ¬ ((List.range' 10 90).all (fun n => isPrime n == isPrime (reverseNum n))) record
  8. reversal_is_involutive_exactly_off_the_trailing_zeros — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => (reverseNum (reverseNum n) == n) == (n % 10 != 0)) record
